# Sign Language Translator — llms.txt

> Free learning aid that converts English text into American Sign Language
> sign sequences. Built and maintained by Firoz Khan of FK Digital Media.

## What this site does

- Text-to-ASL translator: type English text and step through it sign by sign.
  Whole words and phrases are matched against the ASL dictionary first;
  unmatched words are fingerspelled letter by letter (A–Z, 0–9).
- ASL signs dictionary: common words and phrases with step-by-step,
  text-based sign descriptions and practice tips. Searchable, filterable by
  category.
- ASL alphabet & numbers reference: A–Z handshapes (J and Z are motion
  letters) and numbers 0–10.

## Honest limitations (stated on the site itself)

- ASL has its own grammar — word order differs from English. The translator
  shows vocabulary sign by sign; it does not rearrange sentences into ASL grammar.
- This is a learning aid, not a substitute for a qualified interpreter.
  For medical, legal, or emergency communication, use a certified interpreter.
- Sign descriptions are text-based step-by-step guides researched from
  established ASL references (Lifeprint, university and public-health
  materials) and rewritten in original words. Signer-created photos and videos
  are a planned future upgrade. No AI-generated hand images are used.
